patterns.diagnosis: Git can't auto-merge changes in `{1}`. You need to resolve manually.
fixes: Edit to keep the right version, remove the markers.
Then `git add {1}` and `git commit` (or `git merge --continue`).
Abort if you want out: `git merge --abort`.

patterns.title: Detached HEAD
patterns.diagnosis: You checked out a specific commit/tag, not a branch. New commits won't belong to any branch.
fixes: If you want to keep work here: `git switch -c new-branch`.
If you just wanted to peek: `git switch main` to return.

patterns.title: Branch diverged from upstream
patterns.diagnosis: You and the remote each have commits the other doesn't.
fixes: Rebase to put your commits on top: `git pull --rebase`.
Merge if you prefer: `git pull` (creates a merge commit).

patterns.match: nothing to commit, working tree clean
patterns.title: Nothing to commit
patterns.diagnosis: Git sees no changes. Either you didn't edit anything, or the changes aren't staged (or are ignored).
fixes: Check `git status`.
Did your file match `.gitignore`?
Run `git add <files>` if you have unstaged changes.

patterns.title: Empty author identity
patterns.diagnosis: Git needs a name to attribute commits to.
fixes: Set it: `git config --global user.name "Your Name"`.
And email: `git config --global user.email "you@example.com"`.

patterns.match: Please tell me who you are
patterns.title: Identity not configured
patterns.diagnosis: Git needs `user.name` and `user.email` before committing.
fixes: `git config --global user.name "Your Name"`.
`git config --global user.email "you@example.com"`.

patterns.title: Could not read Username (no TTY)
patterns.diagnosis: Git tried to prompt for credentials but there's no terminal.
fixes: Use SSH instead of HTTPS for git remotes.
Configure a credential helper: `git config --global credential.helper store`.
Use a token in the URL (not recommended — leaks in shell history).

patterns.match: The remote end hung up unexpectedly
patterns.title: Remote hung up
patterns.diagnosis: Network dropped or remote rejected the connection.
fixes: Retry — could be transient.
For large pushes, increase buffer: `git config http.postBuffer 524288000`.
Try SSH instead of HTTPS.

patterns.match: error: failed to fetch some refs
patterns.title: Fetch failed
patterns.diagnosis: Some refs couldn't be retrieved from remote.
fixes: Check network connectivity.
Authentication issue? Test with `git ls-remote <url>`.
Specific refs deleted on remote? Try `git fetch --prune`.

patterns.title: Push rejected — file too large
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` exceeds GitHub's 100MB limit.
fixes: Remove the file from history: `git filter-repo` or BFG Repo-Cleaner.
Use Git LFS for large binaries: `git lfs track '*.zip'`.
Add the file to `.gitignore` going forward.

patterns.match: LF will be replaced by CRLF
patterns.title: LF/CRLF line ending warning
patterns.diagnosis: Git's auto-conversion will change line endings on checkout.
fixes: Usually harmless — just a notice.
Configure `core.autocrlf` for your platform (`input` on Linux/Mac, `true` on Windows).
Add `.gitattributes` with explicit line endings for cross-platform repos.

patterns.title: Ambiguous argument
patterns.diagnosis: Git can't tell whether your argument is a branch, file, or ref.
fixes: Use `--` to separate refs from paths: `git checkout HEAD -- file`.
Spell out the full ref: `refs/heads/foo` vs `foo`.

patterns.title: Object file is empty
patterns.diagnosis: An object in `.git/objects/` is corrupt (zero bytes).
fixes: Try `git fsck`.
Delete the bad file and `git fetch` to re-download.
Worst case, re-clone.

patterns.match: git: '([^']+)' is not a git command
patterns.title: git: not a git command — `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` isn't a built-in or installed subcommand.
fixes: Check spelling — `git stauts` → `git status`.
Did you mean one of the suggestions Git printed?
Some commands need extras (`git lfs` needs git-lfs installed).

patterns.title: Submodule has uncommitted changes
patterns.diagnosis: Submodule `{1}` has local edits.
fixes: Enter the submodule and commit/discard those changes.
Or skip with `--ignore-submodules`.

patterns.title: Pre-commit hook failed
patterns.diagnosis: A hook rejected your commit.
fixes: Read the hook output — it usually says exactly what to fix.
Fix and re-stage, then commit again.
Skip the hook only if you know what you're doing: `--no-verify`.

patterns.title: Commit message hook failed
patterns.diagnosis: Your commit message didn't pass the hook (often Conventional Commits or DCO).
fixes: Re-write the message to match the convention.
Common format: `type(scope): description`.

patterns.match: gpg failed to sign the data
patterns.title: gpg failed to sign commit
patterns.diagnosis: Git is configured to GPG-sign but signing failed.
fixes: Check your signing key: `gpg --list-secret-keys`.
Set the right key: `git config user.signingkey <key>`.
Make sure gpg-agent is running.
Disable signing temporarily: `git commit --no-gpg-sign`.

patterns.title: Index lock exists
patterns.diagnosis: Another git process is running, or a stale lock remains.
fixes: Wait for any other git command to finish.
If stale: `rm .git/index.lock`.

patterns.match: Please use -f if you really want to clean
patterns.title: git clean needs -f
patterns.diagnosis: Git won't delete files without confirmation.
fixes: Add `-f`: `git clean -fd`.
Preview first: `git clean -n`.

patterns.match: fatal: A branch named '([^']+)' already exists
patterns.title: Branch already exists — `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: You can't create a branch with a name that's taken.
fixes: Switch to it: `git switch {1}`.
Or pick a new name.
Force-overwrite (destructive): `git branch -f {1}`.

patterns.title: Rebase conflict
patterns.diagnosis: Rebasing hit a conflict.
fixes: Resolve the conflict, then `git add` and `git rebase --continue`.
Skip the offending commit: `git rebase --skip`.
Abort: `git rebase --abort`.

patterns.match: error: The branch '([^']+)' is not fully merged
patterns.title: Branch not fully merged
patterns.diagnosis: Deleting `{1}` would lose commits not on any other branch.
fixes: Make sure those commits are merged elsewhere.
Force-delete if you're sure: `git branch -D {1}`.

patterns.title: Clone destination exists
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` is already there and not empty.
fixes: Pick a different directory: `git clone <url> other-name`.
Or remove the existing directory first.

patterns.match: warning: There are too many unreachable loose objects
patterns.title: Too many loose objects
patterns.diagnosis: Git's storage has accumulated cruft.
fixes: Run `git gc` (garbage collect).
For deeper cleanup: `git gc --aggressive --prune=now`.

patterns.title: Clone failed mid-transfer
patterns.diagnosis: Network dropped or remote sent bad data.
fixes: Retry — usually transient.
Try shallow clone first: `git clone --depth 1`, then fetch the rest.
Increase buffer: `git config http.postBuffer 524288000`.

patterns.match: There is no tracking information for the current branch|no upstream branch
patterns.title: No upstream branch
patterns.diagnosis: This branch isn't tracking a remote, so `git pull` doesn't know where to fetch.
fixes: Set it: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
Or `git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/<branch>`.

patterns.title: Tag already exists
patterns.diagnosis: Tag `{1}` is already in the repo.
fixes: Use a different tag name.
Force-replace (rarely a good idea): `git tag -f {1}`.

patterns.title: No changes added to commit
patterns.diagnosis: You have edits but didn't `git add` them.
fixes: Stage specific files: `git add <files>`.
Or stage everything: `git add -A`.
Use `git commit -a` to stage all tracked changes.

patterns.title: Unmerged paths
patterns.diagnosis: There's an in-progress merge or rebase to finish.
fixes: Resolve the conflicts and `git add` the resolved files.
Continue: `git merge --continue` or `git rebase --continue`.
Abort: `git merge --abort` or `git rebase --abort`.

patterns.match: fatal: unable to access .* Could not resolve host
patterns.title: Couldn't reach git host
patterns.diagnosis: DNS or network can't reach the git remote.
fixes: Check network.
Try `ping github.com`.
Corporate proxy? Configure `http.proxy`.

patterns.match: fatal: unable to access .*: Failed to connect to .* proxy
patterns.title: Git proxy connection failed
patterns.diagnosis: Git's proxy setting points somewhere unreachable.
fixes: Check `git config --get http.proxy`.
Unset if not needed: `git config --global --unset http.proxy`.

patterns.match: fatal: '([^']+)' does not appear to be a git repository
patterns.title: Remote isn't a git repo
patterns.diagnosis: `{1}` URL doesn't point to a repo.
fixes: Double-check the URL.
Authentication failed? Some hosts return 'not a repo' instead of 'access denied'.

patterns.title: ECONNREFUSED — connection refused
patterns.diagnosis: Nothing is listening at that address:port. Server is down or you're hitting the wrong host/port.
fixes: Confirm the server is running.
Verify host and port.
Check firewalls.

patterns.title: ETIMEDOUT — operation timed out
patterns.diagnosis: A network operation took longer than allowed.
fixes: Retry with backoff.
Increase the timeout if appropriate.
Test reachability with `ping` / `curl -v`.

patterns.title: EHOSTUNREACH — no route to host
patterns.diagnosis: The OS can't find a route to the target host.
fixes: Check routing: `traceroute host` or `ip route`.
VPN required? Connect it.
Firewall dropping packets?

patterns.title: ENETUNREACH — network unreachable
patterns.diagnosis: Your machine has no path to that network at all.
fixes: Check that you have a working network interface.
Test with `ping 8.8.8.8`.
VPN or interface down?

patterns.title: EAI_AGAIN — DNS temporary failure
patterns.diagnosis: DNS resolution failed but might succeed if retried.
fixes: Retry after a moment.
Check that your DNS server is reachable.
Try a public resolver (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8).

patterns.title: EAI_NONAME — name unknown
patterns.diagnosis: Hostname doesn't exist in DNS.
fixes: Check spelling.
Confirm the domain resolves: `dig hostname`.
If internal, are you on the right network/VPN?

patterns.title: ENOTFOUND — DNS lookup failed
patterns.diagnosis: Couldn't resolve the hostname.
fixes: Check the URL.
Test with `nslookup`.
Verify DNS settings.

patterns.title: EPIPE — broken pipe
patterns.diagnosis: Wrote to a stream whose reader closed.
fixes: Often harmless — the reader (e.g. `head`) finished early.
Listen for the `error` event on the stream to avoid an unhandled exception.

patterns.title: EISDIR — path is a directory
patterns.diagnosis: You treated a directory as a file.
fixes: Append a filename.
If listing, use `readdir`/`ls` style.

patterns.title: ENOTDIR — not a directory
patterns.diagnosis: Some component of the path is a file, not a directory.
fixes: Inspect the path with `ls -l`.
Did a path concatenation produce something weird?

patterns.title: EEXIST — file already exists
patterns.diagnosis: A create operation hit something that already exists.
fixes: Pick a different name.
Delete the existing file if you mean to replace it.
Use a flag that allows overwriting if available.

patterns.match: ENOSPC: no space left|No space left on device
patterns.title: ENOSPC — disk full
patterns.diagnosis: No free space on the target filesystem.
fixes: Check usage: `df -h`.
Clean caches, logs, old downloads.
Check inodes too: `df -i`.

patterns.title: EROFS — read-only filesystem
patterns.diagnosis: You can't write here — the filesystem is mounted read-only.
fixes: Check the mount with `mount | grep <path>`.
Write somewhere writable (home dir, /tmp).
On macOS, some system paths are read-only by design.

patterns.title: Out of memory
patterns.diagnosis: Process exhausted available RAM and was killed.
fixes: Stream data instead of loading it all into memory.
Increase memory limit (container/VM).
Profile memory use to find leaks.

patterns.title: HTTP 401 — Unauthorized
patterns.diagnosis: Request lacked valid credentials.
fixes: Provide auth headers (token, basic auth).
Token expired? Refresh it.
Check the auth method the API expects.

patterns.title: HTTP 403 — Forbidden
patterns.diagnosis: You're authenticated but not allowed.
fixes: Account may lack permission for this resource.
Some 403s mean the IP/origin is blocked.
Check the response body — it often explains why.

patterns.title: HTTP 404 — Not Found
patterns.diagnosis: The URL doesn't exist on the server.
fixes: Check the path spelling.
Verify the API version in the URL.
Resource may have been deleted or moved.

patterns.title: HTTP 429 — Too Many Requests
patterns.diagnosis: You hit a rate limit.
fixes: Back off and retry after the time in `Retry-After`.
Reduce request rate.
Cache responses to make fewer calls.

patterns.title: HTTP 500 — Internal Server Error
patterns.diagnosis: The server crashed handling your request.
fixes: Not usually your fault — but check whether your input is malformed.
Check the server's logs.
Retry — could be transient.

patterns.title: HTTP 502 — Bad Gateway
patterns.diagnosis: A reverse proxy got a bad response from the upstream server.
fixes: Upstream service may be down or crashing.
Retry — often transient during deploys.
Check upstream health if you own it.

patterns.title: HTTP 503 — Service Unavailable
patterns.diagnosis: Server is overloaded, in maintenance, or has no upstream available.
fixes: Retry with backoff.
Check status page if it's a third-party service.

patterns.title: HTTP 504 — Gateway Timeout
patterns.diagnosis: Reverse proxy gave up waiting for the upstream.
fixes: Upstream is slow or hung.
Increase proxy timeout if you control it.
Optimize the upstream operation.

patterns.match: duplicate key value violates unique constraint
patterns.title: SQL — duplicate key
patterns.diagnosis: Insert/update broke a unique constraint.
fixes: Check the value — does a row with that key exist?
Use `ON CONFLICT` (Postgres) or `INSERT IGNORE` (MySQL).
Use upsert logic where appropriate.

patterns.title: SQL — foreign key violation
patterns.diagnosis: You referenced a row that doesn't exist (or tried to delete a row that's referenced).
fixes: Insert the parent row first.
Or use `ON DELETE CASCADE` if appropriate.
Check ID values match between tables.

patterns.title: SQL — relation `{1}` doesn't exist
patterns.diagnosis: The table/view `{1}` isn't in the current schema.
fixes: Check spelling and schema (`schema.table`).
Run pending migrations.
Maybe you're connected to the wrong database.

patterns.title: SQL — permission denied
patterns.diagnosis: Your DB user lacks privileges on that object.
fixes: `GRANT SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ON <table> TO <user>;`.
Check whether you're connected as the right user.

patterns.match: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon
patterns.title: Docker daemon not reachable
patterns.diagnosis: The Docker daemon isn't running or your user can't talk to it.
fixes: Start Docker: `systemctl start docker` (Linux) or open Docker Desktop.
Linux: add user to `docker` group, then log out and back in.
Check `DOCKER_HOST` env var.

patterns.title: Docker — image not found
patterns.diagnosis: Docker couldn't find the requested image (typo, private registry, or doesn't exist).
fixes: Check spelling and tag.
`docker login` for private registries.
Search: `docker search <name>`.

patterns.match: port is already allocated|bind: address already in use
patterns.title: Docker — port already allocated
patterns.diagnosis: Another container or process is using that port.
fixes: Find: `docker ps` or `lsof -i :PORT`.
Stop the conflicting container or pick a different host port.

patterns.match: permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket
patterns.title: Docker — socket permission denied
patterns.diagnosis: Your user doesn't have access to `/var/run/docker.sock`.
fixes: Add user to docker group: `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER`, then log out/in.
Or run with `sudo` (less ideal).

patterns.title: K8s — ImagePullBackOff
patterns.diagnosis: Kubelet can't pull the container image.
fixes: Check image name and tag in the manifest.
If private registry: add a `imagePullSecrets` to the pod spec.
`kubectl describe pod <pod>` for the underlying error.

patterns.title: K8s — CrashLoopBackOff
patterns.diagnosis: Container starts then crashes repeatedly.
fixes: `kubectl logs <pod> --previous` for the last crash log.
Common causes: bad config, missing env var, app exits immediately.
Check the container's command and args.

patterns.title: K8s — pod stuck Pending
patterns.diagnosis: Pod can't be scheduled. Usually no node with enough resources or missing volumes.
fixes: `kubectl describe pod <pod>` and look at Events.
Check node CPU/memory capacity.
If using PVCs, make sure they're Bound.

patterns.title: K8s — pod OOMKilled
patterns.diagnosis: Container exceeded its memory limit and was killed.
fixes: Raise the memory limit if the app legitimately needs it.
Investigate the memory profile — likely a leak.
Set `requests` and `limits` based on observed usage.

patterns.title: K8s — forbidden for user `{1}`
patterns.diagnosis: RBAC denied the action.
fixes: Check role bindings for `{1}`.
`kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource>` to test.
Bind a role: `kubectl create rolebinding ...`.

patterns.title: SSL handshake failed
patterns.diagnosis: Couldn't agree on TLS parameters with the server.
fixes: Server may require a newer TLS version — update client.
Check the cert isn't expired.
Try `openssl s_client -connect host:443` for details.

patterns.title: SSL cert expired
patterns.diagnosis: The server's TLS certificate is past its valid-until date.
fixes: Server admin needs to renew.
As a temporary client-side workaround for testing, skip verification (don't ship).
Open the URL in a browser to confirm.

patterns.title: SSL — self-signed cert
patterns.diagnosis: The server presents a cert not signed by a trusted CA.
fixes: For dev with self-signed certs: trust the cert in your store.
Don't use `--insecure` / `verify=False` in production.

patterns.title: DNS — NXDOMAIN
patterns.diagnosis: DNS authoritative server says this name doesn't exist.
fixes: Check spelling.
Wait for DNS propagation if you just created the record.
Try a different resolver.

patterns.title: DNS — SERVFAIL
patterns.diagnosis: Resolver couldn't answer because of an upstream problem.
fixes: Try a different DNS server.
Wait a bit — could be transient.
If you own the domain, check DNSSEC and name-server config.

patterns.match: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement
patterns.title: pip — no compatible version
patterns.diagnosis: pip can't find a version of the package that fits your constraints / Python version / platform.
fixes: Check the package supports your Python version.
Loosen any version pin.
Try `--pre` to allow pre-releases.

patterns.title: Disk full
patterns.diagnosis: Out of disk space (or inodes).
fixes: `df -h` to find the full volume.
Clean caches, logs, old containers.
`df -i` to check inode usage.

patterns.title: Too many open files
patterns.diagnosis: Process exceeded FD limit.
fixes: `ulimit -n 4096` to raise.
Close file handles promptly.
Pool connections instead of opening fresh ones each time.

patterns.title: Address already in use
patterns.diagnosis: Another process owns that port.
fixes: Find with `lsof -i :PORT` or `netstat`.
Kill the old process or pick another port.

patterns.title: Disk quota exceeded
patterns.diagnosis: User account hit their disk quota (separate from physical space).
fixes: Clean up your home directory.
Ask admin to raise the quota.

patterns.title: I/O error
patterns.diagnosis: Low-level disk/IO failure.
fixes: Check `dmesg` for hardware errors.
Filesystem may need `fsck`.
If on a network share, check connectivity.

patterns.title: Stale file handle
patterns.diagnosis: On NFS: the file was deleted/replaced from another client.
fixes: Re-open the file.
Reduce `noac`/refresh interval on the NFS mount.

patterns.title: DNS timeout
patterns.diagnosis: DNS server didn't respond in time.
fixes: Try another resolver.
Check network.

patterns.title: TLS protocol version mismatch
patterns.diagnosis: Client and server can't agree on a TLS version.
fixes: Update client (old curl / Python / OpenSSL won't support modern TLS).
Server too old? It may need to support TLS 1.2+.

patterns.title: TLS — unknown issuer
patterns.diagnosis: Server's cert is signed by a CA the client doesn't trust.
fixes: Update CA bundle (`certifi`, system store).
If it's an internal CA, add it to the trust store.

patterns.title: No route to host
patterns.diagnosis: Network has no path to the destination.
fixes: Check routes: `ip route` / `route -n`.
VPN required?
Firewall dropping?

patterns.title: Connection reset by peer
patterns.diagnosis: Remote side sent RST — abrupt close.
fixes: Retry — often transient.
Check server logs for crashes.

patterns.title: Partial write
patterns.diagnosis: Wrote fewer bytes than requested. Often disk full or pipe closed.
fixes: Check disk space.
Loop until all bytes written if writing manually.

patterns.title: File too large
patterns.diagnosis: Exceeds filesystem max file size or process limit.
fixes: Split the file.
Some filesystems (FAT32) have small file-size limits.

patterns.title: Text file busy
patterns.diagnosis: You tried to write to an executable that's currently running.
fixes: Stop the running program first.
Or write to a temp name and rename atomically.

patterns.title: E2BIG — argument list too long
patterns.diagnosis: Same as the bash one — the args don't fit.
fixes: Use `xargs` or `find -exec ... +`.

patterns.title: EINVAL — invalid argument
patterns.diagnosis: A syscall got a bad argument.
fixes: Check the call's parameters.
Some calls fail with EINVAL on certain unsupported flag combos.

patterns.title: ELOOP — symlink loop
patterns.diagnosis: Symlinks form a cycle.
fixes: `readlink -f <path>` to follow.
Break the cycle.

patterns.title: ENOLCK — no locks available
patterns.diagnosis: File locking unavailable (often on network filesystems without locking).
fixes: Use a different filesystem.
Mount NFS with `lock` option.

patterns.title: ENOSYS — not implemented
patterns.diagnosis: The kernel/library doesn't implement that call.
fixes: Library version mismatch?
Containers may filter syscalls — check seccomp profile.

patterns.title: EAGAIN — try again
patterns.diagnosis: Non-blocking call had nothing to return right now.
fixes: Wait and retry, or use `select`/`poll` to wait for readiness.

patterns.title: EINTR — interrupted syscall
patterns.diagnosis: A signal interrupted a blocking call.
fixes: Retry the call.
Most modern libraries handle this for you.

patterns.title: Seccomp blocked operation
patterns.diagnosis: Sandbox blocked a syscall.
fixes: Relax the seccomp profile (carefully).
Run with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` in Docker (only for debugging).

patterns.title: AWS — credentials missing
patterns.diagnosis: AWS SDK can't find credentials.
fixes: Set env vars: `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.
Or configure `~/.aws/credentials`.
Or use an IAM role on EC2/ECS.

patterns.title: AWS — access denied
patterns.diagnosis: IAM denied the call.
fixes: Check the policy attached to the role/user.
Confirm region and account.
Read the error — it usually names the missing permission.

patterns.title: AWS — throttled
patterns.diagnosis: You're calling too fast for the service's limits.
fixes: Use exponential backoff (most SDKs do automatically).
Request a service quota increase if legitimate.

patterns.title: GCP — quota exceeded
patterns.diagnosis: Hit a Google Cloud quota.
fixes: Check quotas in the console.
Request increase if needed.

patterns.title: MongoDB — duplicate key
patterns.diagnosis: Insert/update violated a unique index.
fixes: Use upsert.
Pick a unique value.

patterns.title: Postgres — too many connections
patterns.diagnosis: DB hit its max_connections.
fixes: Use a connection pool (PgBouncer).
Close idle connections.
Raise `max_connections` if hardware can take it.

patterns.title: MySQL — lock wait timeout
patterns.diagnosis: Transaction waited too long for a row lock.
fixes: Shorten transactions.
Look for contended rows / hot keys.
Tune `innodb_lock_wait_timeout`.

patterns.match: ERR max number of clients reached
patterns.title: Redis — max clients reached
patterns.diagnosis: Hit `maxclients`.
fixes: Close idle connections.
Use a pool.
Raise `maxclients` config.

patterns.title: Kafka — offset out of range
patterns.diagnosis: Consumer asked for an offset that's no longer in the topic.
fixes: Reset offset to earliest/latest.
Increase retention if you need older messages.

patterns.title: gRPC — deadline exceeded
patterns.diagnosis: RPC didn't complete within its deadline.
fixes: Increase the deadline if reasonable.
Check why the server is slow.

patterns.title: gRPC — unavailable
patterns.diagnosis: Couldn't reach the gRPC service.
fixes: Check the service address.
Retry — often transient.

patterns.title: OAuth — invalid_grant
patterns.diagnosis: Refresh/auth code rejected. Expired, revoked, or already used.
fixes: Re-authorize from scratch.
Check clock skew on the client (JWT iat/exp).

patterns.title: JWT expired
patterns.diagnosis: Your auth token is past its expiration.
fixes: Refresh the token.
Re-authenticate.

patterns.title: Signature verification failed
patterns.diagnosis: A signed payload didn't verify. Wrong key, tampering, or formatting.
fixes: Confirm both sides use the same key/algorithm.
Don't re-encode the payload between sign and verify.

patterns.title: npm audit — vulnerabilities
patterns.diagnosis: Some dependencies have known security advisories.
fixes: `npm audit fix` to auto-fix what's safe.
Review remaining advisories carefully — not every CVE applies to your use.

patterns.title: Headless Chrome failed to launch
patterns.diagnosis: Puppeteer/Playwright couldn't start the browser.
fixes: Install missing system libraries (most distros need `--no-sandbox` or extras).
Try `--no-sandbox` in args (only in sandboxed envs).
On Linux, install: `libnss3`, `libatk-bridge2.0-0`, etc.

patterns.title: TypeError — int isn't iterable
patterns.diagnosis: You wrote `for x in n:` where `n` is an int. To loop a number of times, use `range(n)`.
fixes: Use `range(n)` to iterate `n` times.
Convert to string `str(n)` to iterate digits.

patterns.match: TypeError: object of type 'int' has no len\(\)
patterns.title: TypeError — int has no len()
patterns.diagnosis: You called `len(n)` on a number.
fixes: Convert to string first: `len(str(n))` to count digits.
Or apply `len` to the actual collection you meant.

patterns.title: zlib error
patterns.diagnosis: Decompression failed — data corrupt or wrong format.
fixes: Verify the source data is actually gzip/zlib compressed.
Check for truncated downloads.

patterns.title: OSError EINVAL
patterns.diagnosis: An OS call got an argument it considered invalid.
fixes: Check path encoding (especially on Windows with non-ASCII).
Some operations need specific flags.

patterns.title: ZeroDivisionError — float division by zero
patterns.diagnosis: You did `x / 0.0` with floats.
fixes: Use `math.inf` or `nan` semantics: `numerator / denom if denom else float('inf')`.

patterns.match: TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting
patterns.title: TypeError — leftover args in % formatting
patterns.diagnosis: Old-style `%` formatting has more args than placeholders.
fixes: Wrap multiple args in a tuple: `'%s %s' % (a, b)`.
Switch to f-strings.

patterns.title: TypeError — number format needed
patterns.diagnosis: `%d`/`%f` got a non-number.
fixes: Convert: `'%d' % int(x)`.

patterns.title: AttributeError — str.decode (Python 3)
patterns.diagnosis: Python 3 strings don't have `.decode` — that's a bytes method.
fixes: If you have bytes, `.decode('utf-8')`.
If you already have a str, you don't need to decode anything.

patterns.title: AttributeError — bytes.encode
patterns.diagnosis: Bytes don't have `.encode`. You probably want `.decode` to get a str.
fixes: Use `.decode('utf-8')` to turn bytes into str.

patterns.title: TypeError — __init__ returned non-None
patterns.diagnosis: `__init__` mustn't return anything other than None.
fixes: Remove the `return` statement.
If you want to construct and return, use `__new__` or a classmethod factory.

patterns.title: decimal — invalid operation
patterns.diagnosis: A `Decimal` operation got bad input or hit a trap.
fixes: Validate the string before constructing `Decimal(s)`.
Set a more lenient `getcontext()` if needed.

patterns.title: React — too many re-renders
patterns.diagnosis: A component keeps calling `setState`/state-setter inside render or in an effect with bad deps, causing an infinite loop.
fixes: Don't call setters unconditionally in the render body.
Check `useEffect` deps — missing them can cause loops.
Memoize functions and values that go into deps.

patterns.match: Can't perform a React state update on an unmounted component
patterns.title: React — setState on unmounted component
patterns.diagnosis: An async callback fired after the component unmounted.
fixes: Track a mounted flag with `useRef` and skip the setter if unmounted.
Cancel pending requests in the effect cleanup.
Use AbortController with fetch.

patterns.match: Functions are not valid as a React child
patterns.title: React — rendered a function
patterns.diagnosis: You rendered a function instead of calling it.
fixes: Call it: `{render()}`, not `{render}`.
If you meant a component, capitalize and use JSX: `<Render />`.

patterns.title: Node engine incompatible
patterns.diagnosis: Module declares Node engines that don't match yours.
fixes: Upgrade Node via `nvm`.
Or pick an older module version that supports your Node.

patterns.title: Node — self-signed cert
patterns.diagnosis: Node rejected a self-signed TLS cert.
fixes: Trust the cert in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.
For dev only: `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` (don't ship!).

patterns.title: EPERM — operation not permitted
patterns.diagnosis: On Windows often a file is open in another process. On Unix, missing capability.
fixes: Close anything that has the file open.
Antivirus on Windows can hold files briefly — retry.

patterns.title: Promise.all needs an iterable
patterns.diagnosis: `Promise.all` got something that isn't iterable.
fixes: Pass an array of promises.
Use `Object.values(map)` if you have an object of promises.

patterns.title: Node deprecation — punycode
patterns.diagnosis: Node has deprecated the built-in `punycode` module.
fixes: Install the userland version: `npm install punycode`.
Or check if your dependency has an update that removes its use.

patterns.title: Git — too many arguments
patterns.diagnosis: Subcommand got more args than it accepts.
fixes: Check the command syntax.
Quote arguments with spaces.

patterns.title: Git — invalid path
patterns.diagnosis: Path `{1}` isn't valid (e.g. contains `..`, or Windows reserved chars).
fixes: Rename the file.
On Windows, watch for `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, etc.

patterns.title: Git rename failed
patterns.diagnosis: Git's working-tree rename failed — usually permissions or a file lock.
fixes: Close anything that has the file open.
Check filesystem permissions.

patterns.title: Git — corrupt loose object
patterns.diagnosis: Object file in `.git/objects/` is damaged.
fixes: Run `git fsck`.
Re-fetch from remote to repair.
Re-clone as a last resort.

patterns.title: Author identity unknown
patterns.diagnosis: Git needs user.name and user.email.
fixes: `git config --global user.name 'You'`.
`git config --global user.email 'you@example.com'`.

patterns.match: The current branch .* has no upstream branch
patterns.title: No upstream — first push
patterns.diagnosis: You haven't set an upstream branch yet.
fixes: `git push -u origin <branch>` to set it on first push.
After that, plain `git push` works.

patterns.title: kill — invalid signal
patterns.diagnosis: Signal name/number isn't recognized.
fixes: List signals: `kill -l`.
Common: `TERM`, `KILL`, `HUP`, `INT`, `QUIT`.

patterns.title: Unterminated command substitution
patterns.diagnosis: `$(...)` or backticks not closed.
fixes: Balance parens / backticks.
Watch for nested substitutions.

patterns.title: pipefail mention
patterns.diagnosis: Pipefail makes pipelines fail when any stage does.
fixes: `set -o pipefail` is recommended at the top of scripts.
Combined with `set -eu` for safer scripts.

patterns.title: Keychain locked
patterns.diagnosis: macOS keychain is locked — you need to unlock it.
fixes: Unlock from Keychain Access app.
`security unlock-keychain`.

patterns.title: HTTP 407 — proxy auth required
patterns.diagnosis: Your proxy needs credentials.
fixes: Set credentials in the proxy URL: `http://user:pass@proxy:port`.
Or configure your client's proxy auth settings.

patterns.title: DNS — REFUSED
patterns.diagnosis: The DNS server refused to answer (likely policy / ACL).
fixes: Try a different resolver.
If you control the server, check its ACLs.

patterns.title: Address family not supported
patterns.diagnosis: Tried to use IPv6 on a system without IPv6, or vice versa.
fixes: Force IPv4: `curl -4`, `python -c 'socket.AF_INET'`.
Check that the interface supports the family.

patterns.title: Tip — setrecursionlimit
patterns.diagnosis: You're raising the recursion limit. Make sure the deep recursion is really intended.
fixes: Verify the algorithm — could it be iterative?
Very deep recursion risks stack overflow at the OS level.

patterns.title: URIError — malformed URI
patterns.diagnosis: `decodeURIComponent` (or similar) got an invalid encoding like `%G1`.
fixes: Validate input before decoding.
Wrap in try/catch and fall back to the raw value.

patterns.title: PendingDeprecationWarning
patterns.diagnosis: A future Python release plans to remove this. You have time, but plan ahead.
fixes: Read the warning text for the replacement.
Bump your code now while it's easy.
